Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:167159
Court No. - 70

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 35532 of 2023
Applicant :- Naveen Kumar

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mamta Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Akash Tomar
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Ms. Mamta Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Vinay Saran, learned Senior
Advocate assisted by Sri Akash Tomar, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Imran Khan,
learned Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
503 of 2023, under Sections 366, 507, 376-D, 384 IPC, Police Station- Kotwali Nagar, District- Bulandshahr, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against unknown person and according to the FIR, marriage of the informant was performed with the prosecutrix about 12 years before and he was having some doubt on the character of his wife and his wife left his house with her paramour and from her matrimonial home, she has taken Rs. 20,000/- and golden jewelleries.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant was not named in the FIR but after seven days when prosecutrix arrived at police station along with her husband i.e. informant of the Naveen Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78214368/
1 case then her statement was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and in the entire statement she made allegation of sexual exploitation and rape against co-accused Sudheer but in the mid of her statement she very casually stated that applicant and one another also committed rape with her.
5.

sentences.text:
He further submitted that when the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then she did not even disclose the name of the applicant and stated that co-accused Sudheer and two other accused persons committed rape with her and from her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. it also reflects that very casually she made allegation of rape against two unknown person along with co-accused Sudheer.
6.
He further submitted that actually applicant runs a medical shop in the house of co-accused Sudheer and only due to this reason, he has been roped in the present mater along with co-accused Sudheer.
7. He further submitted that admittedly prosecutrix is a major and married lady and from the FIR, it reflects that she was having some relationship with another person.
8. He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and is in jail since 02.07.2023.

9. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that it is a case of gang-rape and prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape against the applicant along with co-accused Sudheer and one another person and although, she did not disclose the name of the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. but in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. she also stated that co-accused Sudheer and two unknown persons committed rape with her but as she had already disclosed the identity of the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.,
therefore
, this Court can very well be inferred that out of two unknown persons, one person was applicant.

10. Learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of the informant further submitted that from the medical report dated 19.06.2023, it appears that prosecutrix sustained some abrasions and scratches on her shoulder and fore-arm and this fact suggests that force was applied against her.
11. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

12. From the FIR, it reflects that nobody was named in the FIR and husband of the prosecutrix was having some doubt that his wife is having some relationship with some other person and from the FIR, it also reflects that prosecutrix i.e. wife of the informant according to her own wish had left her matrimonial home but when during investigation after seven days she arrived at police station along with her husband i.e. informant of the case and her statement was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. then she made allegation of sexual exploitation and rape against co-accused Sudheer and also very casually made allegation of rape against applicant and one another person but when her statement was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then she did not even disclose the name of the Naveen Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78214368/
2 applicant and stated that co-accused Sudheer and two unknown persons committed rape with her.

sentences.text: 13. Although, learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of the informant vehemently submitted that as prosecutrix had already disclosed the name of the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., therefore, even if she did not disclose the name of the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then also it can very well be presumed that applicant is one of unknown persons, who committed rape with her

but in criminal law no presumption can be drawn against the accused persons and from the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it reflects that prosecutrix stated that two boys also committed rape with her, therefore, in my view it can not be said on the basis of statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that applicant also committed rape with her.
14. Admittedly prosecutrix is major and married lady and applicant is not having any criminal history.

15. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
16. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

17. Let the applicant- Naveen Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
18. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

19. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 18.8.2023 KK Patel  Naveen Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78214368/
